---------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m1p4t5 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Robots, Bays, MaxOverride

ASSUME Bays \in Nat /\ MaxOverride \in Nat

VARIABLES holder, charging, pending, overridesUsed

vars == <<holder, charging, pending, overridesUsed>>

RobotSeq == CHOOSE s \in [1..Cardinality(Robots) -> Robots] :
              \A r \in Robots : \E i \in 1..Cardinality(Robots) : s[i] = r

N == Cardinality(Robots)

IndexOf(r) == CHOOSE i \in 1..N : RobotSeq[i] = r

NextRobot(r) == RobotSeq[(IndexOf(r) % N) + 1]

TypeOK ==
  /\ holder \in Robots
  /\ charging \subseteq Robots
  /\ pending \subseteq Robots
  /\ overridesUsed \in 0..MaxOverride

Init ==
  /\ holder = RobotSeq[1]
  /\ charging = {}
  /\ pending = {}
  /\ overridesUsed = 0

Request(r) ==
  /\ r \notin pending
  /\ r \notin charging
  /\ pending' = pending \cup {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, charging, overridesUsed>>

PassToken ==
  /\ holder' = NextRobot(holder)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<charging, pending, overridesUsed>>

EnterBay ==
  /\ holder \in pending
  /\ holder \notin charging
  /\ Cardinality(charging) < Bays
  /\ charging' = charging \cup {holder}
  /\ pending' = pending \ {holder}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, overridesUsed>>

AdminForce(r) ==
  /\ overridesUsed < MaxOverride
  /\ r \in pending
  /\ r \notin charging
  /\ Cardinality(charging) < Bays
  /\ charging' = charging \cup {r}
  /\ pending' = pending \ {r}
  /\ overridesUsed' = overridesUsed + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED holder

LeaveBay(r) ==
  /\ r \in charging
  /\ charging' = charging \ {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, pending, overridesUsed>>

Next ==
  \/ PassToken
  \/ EnterBay
  \/ \E r \in Robots : Request(r)
  \/ \E r \in Robots : AdminForce(r)
  \/ \E r \in Robots : LeaveBay(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CapacityRespected == Cardinality(charging) <= Bays

cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Robots = {r1, r2, r3}
  Bays = 2
  MaxOverride = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANTS CapacityRespected
nl:
A fleet of warehouse robots shares a small bank of charging bays. Access to a bay is coordinated by a single circulating token: the robots are arranged in a fixed ring, and the token is passed from each robot to the next one clockwise. Only the robot currently holding the token may move itself from the pending queue into a free charging bay. A robot first signals that it wants to charge (joining the pending set), then waits for the token to reach it before entering. The bank has a fixed number of bays, and a robot already charging can leave at any time, freeing its bay. A human supervisor holds an admin override: a limited number of times, the supervisor may force any waiting robot straight into a free bay without waiting for the token, but even the override still refuses to place a robot when every bay is full. The charging bays are a scarce physical resource, so no matter how tokens circulate, how robots queue, or how often the supervisor intervenes, the number of robots simultaneously charging must never exceed the number of bays.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The count of robots currently occupying charging bays never exceeds the fixed number of bays.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Patrons, Books, MaxEpoch, MaxOverride

ASSUME MaxEpoch \in Nat /\ MaxOverride \in Nat

VARIABLES holds, waiting, epoch, overrides

vars == <<holds, waiting, epoch, overrides>>

HeldBy(b) == {p \in Patrons : <<p, b>> \in holds}

TypeOK ==
  /\ holds \subseteq (Patrons \X Books)
  /\ waiting \in [Books -> SUBSET Patrons]
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ overrides \in 0..MaxOverride

Init ==
  /\ holds = {}
  /\ waiting = [b \in Books |-> {}]
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ overrides = 0

Reserve(p, b) ==
  /\ p \notin waiting[b]
  /\ <<p, b>> \notin holds
  /\ waiting' = [waiting EXCEPT ![b] = @ \cup {p}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holds, epoch, overrides>>

Grant(p, b) ==
  /\ p \in waiting[b]
  /\ HeldBy(b) = {}
  /\ holds' = holds \cup {<<p, b>>}
  /\ waiting' = [waiting EXCEPT ![b] = @ \ {p}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, overrides>>

Return(p, b) ==
  /\ <<p, b>> \in holds
  /\ holds' = holds \ {<<p, b>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, epoch, overrides>>

Reconfigure ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ holds' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, overrides>>

AdminOverride(p, b) ==
  /\ overrides < MaxOverride
  /\ HeldBy(b) = {}
  /\ holds' = holds \cup {<<p, b>>}
  /\ waiting' = [waiting EXCEPT ![b] = @ \ {p}]
  /\ overrides' = overrides + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED epoch

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Patrons, b \in Books : Reserve(p, b)
  \/ \E p \in Patrons, b \in Books : Grant(p, b)
  \/ \E p \in Patrons, b \in Books : Return(p, b)
  \/ \E p \in Patrons, b \in Books : AdminOverride(p, b)
  \/ Reconfigure

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

SingleHolderPerBook ==
  \A b \in Books :
    \A p1, p2 \in Patrons :
      (<<p1, b>> \in holds /\ <<p2, b>> \in holds) => (p1 = p2)

CONSTANTS
  Patrons = {alice, bob, carol}
  Books = {b1, b2}
  MaxEpoch = 2
  MaxOverride = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANTS SingleHolderPerBook
nl:
A university library runs a reservation system for its physical books. Each patron may reserve a title by adding themselves to that title's waiting list. When a book is free, the system may grant it to any patron currently on that book's waiting list; the patron then physically holds the book until they return it. The catalog is periodically reconfigured under a monotonically increasing epoch number (for example, when shelving is reorganized or lost copies are written off); a reconfiguration bumps the current epoch and, because all outstanding loans must be re-validated against the new catalog, it clears every active hold at once. A head librarian has an admin override: they may hand a free book directly to a patron, bypassing the waiting-list order. Regardless of how reservations pile up, how the catalog is reconfigured, or how often the librarian overrides the queue, a single physical copy cannot be in two patrons' hands at the same time.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every book, no two distinct patrons simultaneously hold that book.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od16m0p3t5 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Techs, Slots, Meds, NONE, MaxVersion, MaxOverride

ASSUME MaxVersion \in Nat /\ MaxOverride \in Nat

VARIABLES occupant, version, staged, overrides

vars == <<occupant, version, staged, overrides>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ occupant \in [Slots -> Meds \cup {NONE}]
  /\ version \in [Slots -> 0..MaxVersion]
  /\ staged \in [Techs -> (Slots \X Meds \X (0..MaxVersion)) \cup {NONE}]
  /\ overrides \in 0..MaxOverride

Init ==
  /\ occupant = [s \in Slots |-> NONE]
  /\ version = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
  /\ staged = [t \in Techs |-> NONE]
  /\ overrides = 0

ReadAndStage(t, s, m) ==
  /\ staged[t] = NONE
  /\ occupant[s] = NONE
  /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![t] = <<s, m, version[s]>>]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occupant, version, overrides>>

Commit(t) ==
  /\ staged[t] # NONE
  /\ LET s == staged[t][1] IN
     LET m == staged[t][2] IN
     LET rv == staged[t][3] IN
       /\ occupant[s] = NONE
       /\ version[s] = rv
       /\ version[s] < MaxVersion
       /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![s] = m]
       /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
  /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![t] = NONE]
  /\ UNCHANGED overrides

Abandon(t) ==
  /\ staged[t] # NONE
  /\ LET s == staged[t][1] IN
     LET rv == staged[t][3] IN
       (occupant[s] # NONE \/ version[s] # rv)
  /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![t] = NONE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occupant, version, overrides>>

Pickup(s) ==
  /\ occupant[s] # NONE
  /\ version[s] < MaxVersion
  /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
  /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<staged, overrides>>

AdminPlace(s, m) ==
  /\ overrides < MaxOverride
  /\ occupant[s] = NONE
  /\ version[s] < MaxVersion
  /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![s] = m]
  /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
  /\ overrides' = overrides + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED staged

Idle == UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Techs, s \in Slots, m \in Meds : ReadAndStage(t, s, m)
  \/ \E t \in Techs : Commit(t)
  \/ \E t \in Techs : Abandon(t)
  \/ \E s \in Slots : Pickup(s)
  \/ \E s \in Slots, m \in Meds : AdminPlace(s, m)
  \/ Idle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoStaleOverwrite ==
  \A s \in Slots :
    occupant[s] # NONE =>
      \A t \in Techs :
        staged[t] # NONE => ~(staged[t][1] = s /\ staged[t][3] = version[s])

=============================================================================
nl:
An automated pharmacy fills prescriptions into a bank of numbered pickup slots. Multiple technicians work concurrently, so the dispenser uses optimistic locking to avoid clobbering. To place a filled prescription, a technician first reads a currently-empty slot together with that slot's current version number, staging an intended write (the target slot, the medication, and the version they observed). At most one staged write is outstanding per technician. A staged write commits only if the slot is still empty and its version number still matches the value the technician read; committing places the medication and increments the slot's version. If another operation touched the slot first, the version no longer matches and the technician's staged write is abandoned so they can retry. Picking up a prescription empties the slot and again bumps its version. A pharmacy manager has an admin override that can place a medication into an empty slot directly, also bumping the version. When no technician is acting the dispenser may simply sit idle, leaving its state unchanged. Because every placement bumps the version, an already-filled slot can never have a live staged write whose observed version still matches it, so two technicians can never both dispense into the same slot.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No filled slot ever has an outstanding staged write whose observed version still matches that slot's current version.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od7m7p4t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Cranes, Cap

ASSUME Cap \in Nat /\ Cap > 0

VARIABLES reg, waiting, reading, snapshot

vars == <<reg, waiting, reading, snapshot>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ reg \in 0..Cap
  /\ waiting \subseteq Cranes
  /\ reading \subseteq Cranes
  /\ snapshot \in [Cranes -> 0..Cap]

Init ==
  /\ reg = 0
  /\ waiting = {}
  /\ reading = {}
  /\ snapshot = [c \in Cranes |-> 0]

Arrive(c) ==
  /\ c \notin waiting
  /\ c \notin reading
  /\ waiting' = waiting \cup {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, reading, snapshot>>

ReadRegister(c) ==
  /\ c \in waiting
  /\ c \notin reading
  /\ reading' = reading \cup {c}
  /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![c] = reg]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, waiting>>

CasPlace(c) ==
  /\ c \in reading
  /\ reg = snapshot[c]
  /\ reg < Cap
  /\ reg' = reg + 1
  /\ reading' = reading \ {c}
  /\ waiting' = waiting \ {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED snapshot

CasRetry(c) ==
  /\ c \in reading
  /\ reg # snapshot[c]
  /\ reading' = reading \ {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, waiting, snapshot>>

Depart ==
  /\ reg > 0
  /\ reg' = reg - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, reading, snapshot>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Cranes : Arrive(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cranes : ReadRegister(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cranes : CasPlace(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cranes : CasRetry(c)
  \/ Depart

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

WithinYardCapacity == reg <= Cap

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Cranes = {c1, c2, c3}
  Cap = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANTS WithinYardCapacity
nl:
A container-ship yard has a fixed number of ground stacking slots. Several gantry cranes work the yard concurrently, and they coordinate purely through a single shared register that holds the count of currently occupied slots, updated with compare-and-swap. To land a container, a crane first reads the register, taking a private snapshot of the count it saw. A crane can be slow: an arbitrary amount of time may pass between its read and its attempt, but it never fails outright. When the crane finally attempts its compare-and-swap, it succeeds only if the register still equals its snapshot and there is still room; success atomically increments the register and lands the container. If the register has moved since the crane's read (because another crane got there first), the compare-and-swap fails and the crane discards its snapshot to read again later. A crane requests to work by joining the set of waiting cranes before reading. Containers also depart the yard, atomically decrementing the register. Because the increment only fires when the snapshot still matches and the count is below the limit, the number of occupied slots can never rise above the fixed slot count.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The occupied-slot register never exceeds the total number of stacking slots.

  Jobs = {j1, j2, j3}
  Cap = 2
  MaxTerm = 2
  NONE = NONE
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANTS QueueWithinCapacity
nl:
A print shop runs several spooler nodes in front of one physical printer whose ready queue holds a bounded number of jobs. At any time at most one spooler is the elected leader, and only the leader may admit a job into the printer's ready queue. If there is no leader (for example the previous one crashed), any node may step up and become leader to recover service. A node may also preempt an existing leader by winning a higher election term, up to a bounded number of failovers. Clients submit jobs into a shared unordered pool; because the pool is a set with no ordering, the leader may admit whichever pending job it likes, so admissions need not follow submission order. Admitting a job increments the ready-queue occupancy, and the printer completes jobs one at a time, decrementing it. A leader may fail at any moment, clearing the leadership. No matter how leadership changes hands, how jobs are reordered in the pool, or how failovers interleave, the printer's ready queue never holds more than its fixed capacity of jobs.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of jobs in the printer's ready queue never exceeds the queue's fixed capacity.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od15m2p5t2 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Instances, Brokers, Total, Lot

ASSUME Total \in Nat /\ Lot \in Nat /\ Lot > 0

VARIABLES vote, decision, done, pool

vars == <<vote, decision, done, pool>>

Votes == {"none", "yes", "no"}
Decisions == {"none", "commit", "abort"}

TypeOK ==
  /\ vote \in [Instances -> [Brokers -> Votes]]
  /\ decision \in [Instances -> Decisions]
  /\ done \in [Instances -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ pool \in 0..Total

Init ==
  /\ vote = [i \in Instances |-> [b \in Brokers |-> "none"]]
  /\ decision = [i \in Instances |-> "none"]
  /\ done = [i \in Instances |-> FALSE]
  /\ pool = Total

CastVote(i, b, v) ==
  /\ decision[i] = "none"
  /\ vote[i][b] = "none"
  /\ v \in {"yes", "no"}
  /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![i][b] = v]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<decision, done, pool>>

DecideCommit(i) ==
  /\ decision[i] = "none"
  /\ \A b \in Brokers : vote[i][b] = "yes"
  /\ decision' = [decision EXCEPT ![i] = "commit"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, done, pool>>

DecideAbort(i) ==
  /\ decision[i] = "none"
  /\ \E b \in Brokers : vote[i][b] = "no"
  /\ decision' = [decision EXCEPT ![i] = "abort"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, done, pool>>

Execute(i) ==
  /\ decision[i] = "commit"
  /\ done[i] = FALSE
  /\ pool >= Lot
  /\ done' = [done EXCEPT ![i] = TRUE]
  /\ pool' = pool - Lot
  /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, decision>>

Idle == UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
  \/ \E i \in Instances, b \in Brokers, v \in Votes : CastVote(i, b, v)
  \/ \E i \in Instances : DecideCommit(i)
  \/ \E i \in Instances : DecideAbort(i)
  \/ \E i \in Instances : Execute(i)
  \/ Idle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

PoolMatchesCrosses ==
  pool = Total - Lot * Cardinality({i \in Instances : done[i]})

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Instances = {aucA, aucB}
  Brokers = {br1, br2}
  Total = 2
  Lot = 1
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANTS PoolMatchesCrosses
nl:
A stock exchange runs its opening auction as a two-phase commit across the participating brokers. Two independent auction instances (two symbols crossing at the bell) run at once, but they draw executable shares from one shared inventory pool. In each instance, the coordinator collects a prepare vote from every broker: a broker votes yes or no while the instance is still undecided. Once all brokers in an instance have voted yes, the coordinator may decide to commit; if any broker votes no, the coordinator may decide to abort. Committing enables the irreversible action: the instance prints its cross exactly once, marking itself done and withdrawing its fixed lot of shares from the shared pool. The cross is irreversible, so an instance that has already printed can never print again, and the pool is only ever debited by the lot for each instance that has crossed. Before the bell, or once both instances have settled, the exchange may simply sit idle. Because the shared pool is debited exactly one lot per crossed instance and matches the set of instances that have crossed, no instance's cross can ever fire more than once.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The shared pool always equals the starting total minus one lot for each distinct instance that has crossed, so no cross prints twice.

ASSUME MaxTerm \in Nat

VARIABLES leader, term, slotOf, waiting

vars == <<leader, term, slotOf, waiting>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ leader \in Controllers \cup {NONE}
  /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
  /\ slotOf \in [Cars -> Slots \cup {NONE}]
  /\ waiting \subseteq Cars

Init ==
  /\ leader = NONE
  /\ term = 0
  /\ slotOf = [c \in Cars |-> NONE]
  /\ waiting = {}

Elect(ctrl) ==
  /\ leader = NONE
  /\ leader' = ctrl
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, slotOf, waiting>>

Preempt(ctrl) ==
  /\ leader # NONE
  /\ ctrl # leader
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ leader' = ctrl
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slotOf, waiting>>

LeaderFail ==
  /\ leader # NONE
  /\ leader' = NONE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, slotOf, waiting>>

RequestWash(car) ==
  /\ car \notin waiting
  /\ slotOf[car] = NONE
  /\ waiting' = waiting \cup {car}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, slotOf>>

AssignSlot(ctrl, car, s) ==
  /\ leader = ctrl
  /\ car \in waiting
  /\ slotOf[car] = NONE
  /\ \A c \in Cars : slotOf[c] # s
  /\ slotOf' = [slotOf EXCEPT ![car] = s]
  /\ waiting' = waiting \ {car}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term>>

ReleaseSlot(car) ==
  /\ slotOf[car] # NONE
  /\ slotOf' = [slotOf EXCEPT ![car] = NONE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, waiting>>

Next ==
  \/ \E ctrl \in Controllers : Elect(ctrl)
  \/ \E ctrl \in Controllers : Preempt(ctrl)
  \/ LeaderFail
  \/ \E car \in Cars : RequestWash(car)
  \/ \E ctrl \in Controllers, car \in Cars, s \in Slots : AssignSlot(ctrl, car, s)
  \/ \E car \in Cars : ReleaseSlot(car)

  Cardinality({c \in Cars : slotOf[c] # NONE})
    = Cardinality({slotOf[c] : c \in Cars} \ {NONE})

nl:
A car-wash conveyor line has a set of numbered wash slots. Several controller units can run the line, but only one is the elected leader at a time; if there is no leader any controller may step up, and a controller may preempt the current leader by winning a higher election term, up to a bounded number of failovers. A leader may also fail, clearing leadership. Cars arriving to be washed drop their tickets into a shared unordered request pool, so the leader may pick any waiting car to service next rather than following arrival order. When the leader assigns a waiting car to a wash slot, it only ever picks a slot that no car currently holds, and the car then occupies that slot until its wash finishes and it releases the slot. Because assignment always targets a currently-free slot, the mapping from cars to their slots stays one-to-one: the number of cars holding a slot always equals the number of distinct slots in use. No matter how leadership changes or how the request pool is reordered, a single wash slot is never allocated to two different cars at once.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No wash slot is ever allocated to two different cars simultaneously.

  /\ record \in 0..Cardinality(Drones)
  /\ staged \in [Drones -> (0..Cardinality(Drones)) \cup {NONE}]
  /\ contributed \subseteq Drones

  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, record, staged, contributed>>

  /\ d # holder
  /\ members' = members \ {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, record, staged, contributed>>

  /\ staged[holder] = NONE
  /\ d \in members
  /\ d # holder
  /\ holder' = d
  /\ UNCHANGED <<members, record, staged, contributed>>

  /\ d \notin contributed
  /\ staged[d] = NONE
  /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![d] = record]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<members, holder, record, contributed>>

  /\ staged[d] # NONE
  /\ record' = staged[d] + 1
  /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![d] = NONE]

  /\ UNCHANGED <<members, holder>>

  \/ \E d \in Drones : Leave(d)
  \/ \E d \in Drones : PassToken(d)

CONSTANTS
  Drones = {d1, d2, d3}
  NONE = NONE
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANTS NoLostUpdate
nl:
A swarm of wildfire surveillance drones maintains one shared situation record (a running tally of confirmed hotspots). To keep concurrent edits from clobbering each other, the swarm circulates a single token around a ring, and only the drone currently holding the token may edit the shared record. The swarm's size changes at runtime: drones may join the ring, and drones other than the current token-holder may leave. The token may be passed to any other current member, but only when the holder is not in the middle of an edit. A drone edits the record with a read-modify-write: while holding the token and not yet having contributed, it first reads the record's current value into a private staging register, then writes back that value plus one, recording its contribution and clearing its staging register. Because the token is exclusive and the holder cannot pass it away while an edit is staged, the value a drone read is always still the record's current value when it writes, so no update is ever silently lost. No matter how the swarm grows or shrinks or how the token circulates, any staged read still matches the live record.

  /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, log, crashed>>

AcquireFine(w, u) ==
  /\ w \notin crashed
  /\ coarse[FridgeOf(u)] = w
  /\ fine[u] = NONE
  /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![u] = w]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, log, crashed>>

  /\ coarse[FridgeOf(u)] = w
  /\ fine[u] = w

  \/ \E w \in Workers, u \in Units : AcquireFine(w, u)

A blood bank tracks individual blood units stored across several refrigerators. An airport baggage router commits each batch of routing decisions using two-phase commit across its handling stations. Each 2PC batch runs in a numbered round.
